"BUILD A NEW ONLINE RPG – CHARACTER CREATION AND GAME FOUNDATION

First inspect the project environment, available tools and backend capabilities. Then start building a playable RPG foundation.

1. Character creation

- Players can choose between a male and female character.
- Create a character customization screen.
- Include at least 3 different hairstyles.
- Eye colors: blue, green and brown.
- Include 3 different starting equipment color styles.
- Players can preview their character before confirming.
- Cosmetic choices must not affect combat stats.
- Keep the appearance system expandable for future cosmetics and skins.

2. Classes and equipment

- Create multiple distinct character classes with unique abilities and playstyles.
- Each class has its own weapons and armor.
- Some equipment can only be used by specific classes.
- Equipment must have minimum level requirements.
- Include equipment stats, rarity and upgrade possibilities.
- Display clearly when an item cannot be equipped because of class or level restrictions.

3. Core gameplay

- Character levels, experience and player statistics.
- Inventory and equipment management.
- Real-time combat with monsters.
- Monster health, damage and rewards.
- Gold and item drops.
- A beautiful starting world with NPCs, quests and explorable areas.
- Save and load player progress.

4. Drop chances and numerical systems

Create a configurable loot system with these initial rarity chances:

- Common: 60%
- Uncommon: 25%
- Rare: 10%
- Epic: 4%
- Legendary: 0.9%
- Mythic: 0.1%

Total: 100%.

Include:

- Different loot tables for different monsters.
- Special boss drops.
- Unique weapons and armor.
- Crafting materials.
- Rare cosmetic drops.
- Configurable drop chances.
- At least 100,000 simulated loot rolls to test the probabilities.

All important game values must be centrally configurable. Use mathematical calculations to keep the game balanced.

5. Technical requirements

- Build modularly with clean, maintainable code.
- Inspect available backend capabilities before implementing online features.
- Never pretend simulated online features are real multiplayer.
- Protect important game data from client-side manipulation where server functionality is available.
- Test character creation, movement, combat, inventory, equipment restrictions and loot.
- Fix bugs before reporting completion.

Start implementing the game now. Do not stop after writing a design document. Create the actual playable game and test the implemented features.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.
"
